subject: Dedicated pool SLO carveout / queueing behavior — Magnetica request
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@magnetica.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@magnetica.ai>, Magnetica Legal <legal@magnetica.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Dedicated pool SLO clarification & carveout

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're moving toward a Dedicated pool commitment (MAG-472) but a couple of constraints on our side mean we need a short carveout to the standard queueing behavior and throughput guarantee during our nightly post-process window (00:00–02:30 PT).

Specifically:
- For the 2.5 hour nightly window we run large batched prompts that create significant KV cache churn; to avoid failed runs we need a soft-priority lane ensuring in-flight concurrency for those jobs (approx 40 concurrent requests, avg 1.6k tokens per request).
- We understand Redwood's normal queueing will evict or preempt some jobs when demand peaks. We are requesting an "inflight headroom carveout" (temporary increase to reserved headroom) for Q4 ramp, or an explicit SLO exception window with credits if throughput drops below the reserved baseline.
- We also need traceable observability (per-request latency percentiles and queue-depth metrics) for troubleshooting.

Attached is our Q4 capacity forecast. Can your team advise on whether this is handled via an SLA amendment, a temporary carveout, or a dedicated priority lane config? We are on a timeline to sign the Reserved GPU commitment by 10/31.

Appreciate your help — Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, Magnetica
attachment: magnetica-capacity-forecast-Q4.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@magnetica.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated pool SLO clarification & carveout

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the forecast and clear ask. Short answer: we can support a temporary carveout but it requires alignment across Product/SRE and Legal for the amendment language and credits. Looping in Ben and Karthik to scope the technical approach and Olga for contract language.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to propose commercial amendment options (credits vs scheduled carveout).
2) Karthik to validate feasible technical configurations (soft-priority lane vs short-lived headroom).
3) Legal to draft a short SLA addendum for the Q4 window if needed.
4) Quick sync (30m) with your platform lead to confirm traffic patterns.

Ben/Karthik/Olga — can you review and share availability for a call tomorrow (10/21)?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Driving reliable inference at scale

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@magnetica.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated pool SLO clarification & carveout

Sanjay — thanks for the details. Quick commercial framing so the legal team has options:

Option A — Temporary SLO exception window (preferred):
- Define explicit window(s) for the carveout (e.g., daily 00:00–02:30 PT, 11/01–12/31).
- During the window, Redwood will apply a soft-priority lane that increases inflight headroom to accommodate your batch jobs up to the committed reserved capacity plus a 15% temporary headroom.
- If effective throughput (tokens/sec) for reserved capacity falls below the baseline outside normal maintenance, Magnetica will receive a one-time credit equal to X% of that day's usage (draft amounts in attachment).

Option B — Scheduled maintenance carveout (lower operational risk):
- Reserve a nightly reserved burst slice (e.g., 30 minutes within the window) where preemption is disabled for tagged Magnetica jobs.

Operational notes:
- We'll need your jobs to include a short metadata tag so the runtime can route to the soft-priority lane without manual intervention.
- Observability: we can provision a per-route metrics feed (p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, inflight concurrency) and share a read-only dashboard.

I've attached a first-draft amendment template and a queueing diagram to illustrate. Happy to walk through on a call — propose Thu 10/22 10:00 AM PT.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachment: slo-exception-draft-redwood.docx (docx)
attachment: dedicated-pool-queueing-diagram.png (png)

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@magnetica.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@magnetica.ai>, Magnetica Legal <legal@magnetica.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated pool SLO clarification & carveout

Ben / Rachel —

Thanks — Option A aligns best with our internal ops. A couple of clarifications before the call:
- Can the temporary headroom be increased to 25% for peak holiday runs (we expect two weeks of elevated batch volume mid-November)?
- For credits, we prefer per-incident throughput credits rather than a daily bucket — easier to map to our billing.

We're happy to tag jobs; Priya will work with your infra team on the tagging key. Confirming Thu 10/22 10:00 AM PT for the sync.

— Sanjay

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@magnetica.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 13:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Dedicated pool SLO clarification & carveout

Folks — follow-up from our technical sync and lab validation:

Summary of what we can implement before your Q4 ramp:
- Soft-priority lane: runtime will accept a job tag (header: X-Redwood-Priority: magnetica-batch) and place it into a separate inflight pool. This pool is backed by the same reserved GPUs but uses token-aware admission to maintain baseline tail-latency SLOs for interactive traffic.
- Headroom limits: we can provision a temporary headroom of up to 25% for two specified weeks and 15% for the remainder of the carveout window.
- Queueing behavior: preemption will be disabled for tagged jobs while they are in the inflight pool; if system-wide contention exceeds a fail threshold, we will trigger an automatic graceful-degrade policy (spill to delayed queue with X-min retry and notify Magnetica).
- Observability: we'll expose per-route metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, inflight count, queue depth) and provide a read-only Grafana link plus a daily digest during the carveout.

Technical caveats:
- Temporary headroom consumes shared reserved capacity — sustained overrun may affect other tenants if not bounded.
- We will require your tagging, and a short runbook for our on-call to expedite troubleshooting during the two peak weeks.

I'll add the configuration snippets to the OPS ticket (OPS-3241) and attach them to the amendment.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@magnetica.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Magnetica Legal <legal@magnetica.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated pool SLO clarification & carveout — next steps

Sanjay —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the productive call. Per the discussion we will:
- Produce a short SLA addendum that defines the carveout window (11/01–12/31, nightly 00:00–02:30 PT) with two elevated weeks (11/15–11/28) at 25% headroom.
- Amendment will include per-incident throughput credits (mechanic in draft).
- Karthik will push the config snippets to OPS-3241 and we will provision the read-only dashboard for your team.
- Olga will circulate the amendment for signature; Ben and I will run procurement logistics.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Olga: first draft of SLA addendum (initial by 10/29).
- Ben: commercial credit table and DocuSign link (initial by 10/29).
- Karthik: push config & observability endpoint to OPS ticket (done by 10/27 — posted).
- Priya (Magnetica): provide job-tagging key and test plan (by 10/30).

If that timeline works we'll include the addendum in the main Reserved GPU contract before your sign date.

Thanks — look forward to getting this across the finish line.

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
